native_result.query: The effect of which variable on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024 to 0.0923 (while becoming insignifcant) when both SES and academic characteristics are included in analysis?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636  (significant) to  -0.2293 (insignificant) and effect of race on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024  (significant) to 0.0923 (insignificant) when academic characteristics are considered.
native_result.HypoB: The variable whose effect on BA degree completion falls to ~0.0923 (log-odds, OR≈1.10) and becomes statistically insignificant (p=0.68, 95% CI −0.35 to 0.53) once SES and academic characteristics are both included is SAMPLE_RACE — being Black (vs White; Hispanic the other category). Black students' large significant BA-completion disadvantage (unadjusted log-odds ≈ −1.01, OR≈0.37, p<0.001; 1.3% Black vs 3.5% White) is eliminated when the SES index plus ASVAB ability and class percentile are controlled, indicating the Black–White BA-completion gap is explained by SES and academic preparation rather than an independent race effect. The 0.5024 baseline is not reproducible by any defensible model on this dataset; identification rests on the exact 0.0923 endpoint (matched to 0.0003) and uniqueness of the significant-to-insignificant flip.
